column4: The Holy Spirit is not a new spirit but is of God and has been with God since the very beginning. In Genesis 1:2 the Spirit of God is hovering on the waters during creation. In Nehemiah 9:20, the scriptures say that it was the Spirit who instructed the people in the wilderness. It was by this same Holy Spirit that God anointed the kings, judges, and prophets in the Old Testament. In Joel 2:28-29 the Spirit is promised to be poured out on all mankind. It was by this same Holy Spirit that God raised Jesus from the dead, and now dwells in us (Romans 8:11). There is only one Holy Spirit, and He has always been the same. How He works with people has looked different at different times, but His heart has never changed.
column5: The Holy Spirit is not a new spirit but is of God, and was with God from the beginning. In Genesis 1:2, at creation the Spirit of God was moving over the waters. In Nehemiah 9:20, the Bible says it was the Spirit who taught and led the people in the wilderness. In the Old Testament, God anointed kings, judges, and prophets with this same Holy Spirit. In Joel 2:28-29, it is promised that the Spirit will be poured out on all people. By this same Holy Spirit God raised Jesus from the dead, and He now dwells in us（Romans 8:11）. The Holy Spirit is one and always the same. The way He engages with people may appear different from age to age, but His will never changes.

column4: In John 20, after His resurrection, Jesus appears to His disciples in the middle of a locked room and breathes on them saying ‘*Receive the Holy Spirit*’ (John 20:22). This was not, however when they received the Spirit of God upon them, empowering them with boldness for ministry. This was when they received the Holy Spirit within them, allowing them to abide and commune with God. This will be discussed at greater depth later in this chapter as well as the chapters on sanctification and baptism.
column5: In John chapter 20, after the resurrection, Jesus appeared to His disciples in the middle of a locked room, breathed on them, and said, “Receive the Holy Spirit” (John 20:22). There is theological debate about exactly what happened at that moment, but many Pentecostal interpretations view this as the event in which the disciples received the Spirit of God within, signifying regeneration—being born again. However, this was not the event in which the Spirit of God came upon them to empower them with boldness for ministry. This was when they received the Holy Spirit within, enabling them to abide in God and have fellowship with Him. We will address this in more detail later in this chapter and in the chapters on Sanctification and Baptism.

column4: The Holy Spirit is first and foremost, from and of God. The scriptures refer to the Spirit as the Spirit of God, or the Spirit of the Lord, or the Spirit of Christ, while these highlight different aspects, they are all one in the same. The Holy Spirit, being fully God, is also eternal and is holy (blameless, innocent, pure, not profane). Some translations refer to the Holy Spirit as the Holy Ghost.
column5: Above all, the Holy Spirit is the one who comes from God and belongs to God。 The Bible calls the Holy Spirit the Spirit of God, the Spirit of the Lord, or the Spirit of Christ。 These emphasize different aspects, but they all refer to the same person。 The Holy Spirit is fully God, and also eternal, holy（blameless, innocent, pure, not profane）です。 In some translations, the Holy Spirit is called the Holy Ghost。

column4: The word spirit in Greek is **Pneuma** (**NYOO-mah** - **G4151**), it means breath, or wind. The Hebrew word for spirit means the same. Breath is significant as we need it in constant supply to live. It was God's breath that He blew into Adam to bring Him to life, likewise it was Jesus' breath that He breathed last before He died on the cross. Without breath there is no life. Breath like wind can be felt and experienced but are not as easily observed as other ‘elements’ water, fire, earth.
column5: In Greek, the word for “spirit” is **Pneuma**（**NYOO-mah** - **G4151**）, meaning breath, wind。 The Hebrew word for spirit has the same meaning。 Breath is important because we constantly need it to live。 It was God’s breath that He breathed into Adam to give him life, and likewise, it was that breath that Jesus finally yielded before He died on the cross。 Without breath there is no life。 Breath can be felt and experienced like the wind, but it is not as easily observed as the other “elements” such as water, fire, and earth。

column5: The Holy Spirit testifies of Jesus, exalts Jesus, teaches, brings to remembrance Jesus’ teachings (John 14:26), and also guides us into all truth (John 16:13). Similarly, in Acts 16:16-18, a slave girl’s words about Paul and Silas were accurate but inspired by a demonic spirit, not the Holy Spirit. These examples remind us that even words that seem true can originate from ungodly sources.
column5: Throughout Scripture we find examples of false claims. Often they come from false prophets, or from people who, even if well-intentioned, spoke against the will of God. Similarly, Acts 16:16-18 shows that the words a slave girl spoke about Paul and Silas were accurate, but they were inspired not by the Holy Spirit, but by an evil spirit. These examples remind us that words which seem plausible and true can still come from ungodly sources.

column4: Diving deeper, the Spirit brings conviction of these three truths:
column5: Going further, the Holy Spirit brings conviction regarding the following three truths:

column4: 1.  **Conviction of sin**: Revealing the reality of human rebellion against God, drawing men’s attention to the depravity of their own lives.
column5: 1.  **Conviction of sin**: making clear the reality that humans are in rebellion against God, and directing people’s attention to the corruption of their own lives.

column4: 2.  **Conviction of righteousness**: Demonstrating Jesus’ perfect fulfillment of the Father’s will, and that Jesus' sacrifice provided the one-time atonement needed for forgiveness of sins.
column5: 2.  **Conviction of righteousness**: showing that Jesus perfectly fulfilled the Father’s will, and that Jesus’ sacrifice provided the once-for-all atonement required for the forgiveness of sins.

column4: 3.  **Conviction of judgment**: Affirming the defeat of Satan, the certainty of God’s justice, and that all will stand a judgement for their life's work and deeds.
column5: 3.  **Conviction of judgment**: affirming Satan’s defeat, the certainty of God’s justice, and that all will be judged for the works and deeds of their lives.

column4: The Holy Spirit brings supernatural boldness to proclaim the witness of the Gospel in the face of persecution. The outcome of this empowerment can be described, but it's best experienced. People are healed physically and emotionally, the dead raised, those tormented by evil spirits are set free, people with hard hearts turn and repent.
column5: The Holy Spirit brings a supernatural boldness to proclaim the testimony of the gospel even in the face of persecution. This missional boldness is often accompanied by supernatural acts through manifestations of the Spirit and power (1 Corinthians 2:1-5). People are healed physically and emotionally, the dead are raised, those tormented by evil spirits are set free, and those with stubborn hearts turn and repent.

column4: ## Building a Relationship with the Holy Spirit
column5: ## Building a Relationship with the Holy Spirit

column4: Every relationship takes time and experience to develop deeply. The Holy Spirit is our advocate, our comforter, our helper, and our guide. He empowers us and sanctifies us.
column5: Every relationship needs time and experience to grow deep. The Holy Spirit is our advocate, comforter, helper, and guide. The Holy Spirit empowers us and sanctifies us.

column4: Start to think of the Holy Spirit as you would a person. In our relationship we can both work to build it or do things that weaken our relationship. He can be ignored, He can be quenched, He can be blasphemed, or He can be listened to, honored, and obeyed.
column5: Begin to think of the Holy Spirit as a person. In a relationship, we can build it together or do things that weaken it. The Holy Spirit can be ignored, quenched, or blasphemed, and he can also be listened to, honored, and obeyed.

column4: Don’t ignore the voice of the Holy Spirit. He is always speaking to us and the church. If you don’t yet know how to distinguish the voice of the Holy Spirit, it takes time, willingness, and effort (like all healthy and beneficial relationships). But don’t worry, you already have built into you all the necessary parts needed to start to develop a personal relationship with the Holy Spirit.
column5: Do not ignore the voice of the Holy Spirit. The Holy Spirit is always speaking to us and to the Church. If you don’t yet know how to discern the voice of the Holy Spirit, it takes time, willingness, and effort (just like any healthy, beneficial relationship). But don’t worry. Everything you need to begin building a personal relationship with the Holy Spirit is already within you.

column4: The quickest and most reliable ways to build an effective relationship with the Holy Spirit is to
column5: The quickest and surest ways to build an effective relationship with the Holy Spirit are

column4: 1.  Call out to Him **individually** in prayer, pause and wait for Him to speak.
column5: 1.  In prayer, call out to the Holy Spirit **personally**, pause, and wait for him to speak.

column4: 2.  Call out to Him as part of a **group** of people who know Him (the church), pause, and wait for Him to speak.
column5: 2.  As part of a **group** of people who know him (the Church), call out to the Holy Spirit, pause, and wait for him to speak.

column4: I use the phrase ‘call out’ to mean literally, with your mouth, or however you speak (with your hands if you cannot speak aloud with your mouth). Why speak? A few reasons:
column5: I use the term ‘call out’ to mean literally speaking with your mouth, or communicating in whatever way you speak (with your hands if you cannot speak out loud). Why speak? There are several reasons:

column4: 1.  We are speaking spirits made in God's image. God speaks, and so do we.
column5: 1.  We are speaking spirits made in the image of God. God speaks, and we speak.

column4: 2.  We use speaking as the primary way to communicate. You can also write down what you want to say (journaling) and speak it aloud.
column5: 2.  We use speaking as our primary means of communication. You can also write down what you want to say (journaling) and read it aloud.

column4: 3.  Speaking is an intentional act, and indicates to the party you are talking to, that you’d like to engage them in a conversation.
column5: 3.  Speaking is an intentional act and signals to the one you’re addressing that you want to have a conversation.

column4: #### What should you say?
column5: #### What should you say?

column4: If you’ve never talked to God, try introducing yourself. Sure, it will feel a bit weird, but that discomfort is okay and temporary. Along with introducing yourself, tell God that you want to talk to Him and that you want Him to talk back to you.
column5: If you’ve never spoken to God, try introducing yourself. It will certainly feel a bit strange, but that awkwardness is okay and temporary. In addition to introducing yourself, tell God what you want to talk about, and that you would like him to speak back to you as well.

column4: Consider asking Him a question. It doesn’t have to be a deep theological question; it can start simple. Can you show me Your love for me? Why do I have a certain feeling? What would You like to tell me?
column5: Consider asking God questions. They don’t need to be deep theological questions. You can start with simple ones. Could you show me your love for me? Why am I feeling a certain way? What do you want to say to me?

column4: #### Then what?
column5: #### What next?

column4: Well in all effective relationships you speak for a bit, then you pause and listen. God will speak.
column5: In an effective relationship, after speaking a little, you pause and listen. God speaks.

column4: God speaks in many ways, but He wants to do it personally, and internally. It will likely not be an audible voice (like if your best friend was to say your name aloud) but it will be an internal voice that speaks to your heart and mind. Elijah refers to this as the ‘still small voice’ (1 Kings 19:11-13).
column5: God speaks in many ways, but he desires to speak personally and internally. It will likely not be an audible voice (like your best friend calling your name out loud), but an inner voice that speaks to your heart and thoughts. Elijah calls this a ‘still small voice’ (1 Kings 19:11-13).

column4: The most common ways that I've personally witnessed God talk to people, and I've been blessed to help dozens of people learn how to talk to God directly, is some combination of the following:
column5: The most common ways I have personally witnessed God speaking to people (I’ve been fortunate to help dozens learn how to talk with God directly) are some combination of the following:

column4: - A knowing - the person talking to God gets an immediate understanding that helps them.
column5: - A sense of knowing - the person who is speaking to God receives an immediate, helpful understanding.

column4: - A picture - also known in the scriptures as a vision or a dream (a vision is when you are awake, a dream is when you are asleep), God will give you a picture in your mind. Perhaps it’s a memory, or place you’ve been or know? Explore the picture, what do you see? What do you feel as a result? What’s happening?
column5: - Images - also called visions and dreams in the Bible (visions when you are awake, dreams when you are asleep). God gives images to your mind. It may be a memory, or a place you have been or know. Explore the image. What do you see? As a result, what do you feel? What is happening?

column4: - An inner voice - like an audible voice, but one that only you can hear, and spoken into your heart and mind.
column5: - Inner voice - It is like an actual audible voice, yet only you can hear it, and it speaks to your heart and mind.

column4: #### What will God say?
column5: #### What would God say?

column4: Not sure! But that’s the fun in it. I can say that He is NOT the spirit of fear, but of perfect love and that it will never violate the teaching of the scriptures. E.g., God will never tell you to commit an extra-marital affair.
column5: We don't know for sure! But that's the interesting part. We can at least say this: He is not a spirit of fear but of perfect love, and what He speaks will never contradict the teaching of Scripture. For example, God will never tell you to commit adultery.

column4: Now what?
column5: So, what do you do next?

column4: Keep the dialogue going! It’s really that simple.
column5: Keep the conversation going! That's really all there is to it.

column4: ### Why build a relationship?
column5: ### Why build a relationship?

column4: The Holy Spirit is the Helper. The Helper helps us! The work goes much more smoothly if we have a shared language, and relationship with Him. Can you imagine trying to work with someone in your job if you had no relationship, did not speak the same language, and couldn't communicate?!
column5: The Holy Spirit is the Helper. The Helper helps us! If we share a common language and have a relationship with the Holy Spirit, the work will go much more smoothly. Can you imagine working with someone at work with whom you have no relationship, don't speak the same language, and can't communicate?!

column4: We serve a God who wants to communicate with us. Jesus said that His sheep know His voice (John 10:27), we have built into us all already the natural abilities we need, but we may lack experienced proficiency.
column5: The God we serve desires to converse with us. Jesus said that His sheep know His voice (John 10:27). We already possess the natural faculties we need, though we may lack the proficiency that comes with experience.

column4: Speaking from personal experience, a personal and active relationship with the Holy Spirit is one of the best things about being a Christian. His presence brings us peace, comfort, and direction, but only if you know how to seek, listen, and obey Him.
column5: From personal experience, a personal and vibrant relationship with the Holy Spirit is one of the best gifts of being a Christian. His presence brings peace, comfort, and direction, but only when you know how to seek, hear, and obey His voice.

column4: Develop a sensitivity with the Holy Spirit. Like many married people over time, you can communicate with your spouse in a unique way and sometimes just through a look. The look alone tells you everything you need to know about what just happened and what's going to happen. Build that type of sensitivity and familiarity with the Holy Spirit. Include Him in your whole life, this is a wonderful part of your relationship with Him that will provide so much depth and richness to your walk of faith.
column5: Cultivate sensitivity to the Holy Spirit. As happens with many couples over the years, you can communicate with your spouse in a unique way, sometimes with just a glance. From that single look, you know what has happened, what is about to happen, everything that is needed. Build that same sensitivity and intimacy with the Holy Spirit. Welcome Him into every part of your life. This is a wonderful aspect of the relationship that will add depth and richness to your walk of faith.

column4: The Holy Spirit has come to lead us and guide us, to empower us to be God’s people, and to see the people of the Earth radically transformed, delivered from the kingdom of darkness into the kingdom of light. Getting to know him, building trust with Him is essential to everyday life and to accomplish the work that Jesus has for us to do.
column5: The Holy Spirit came to guide us, empower us to live as God's people, and to see people on earth fundamentally transformed and set free from the kingdom of darkness into the kingdom of light. Knowing the Holy Spirit and building trust with Him is essential both for daily life and for accomplishing the work Jesus has entrusted to us.

column5: 1.  In what ways have you experienced the Holy Spirit as Comforter, Guide, or source of power? Which role resonates most in this season of your life?

column5: 2.  Consider the difference between the Holy Spirit being "within" (an inward work) and "upon" (an outward work). How does that distinction affect your understanding of the Holy Spirit's work in your life?

column5: 3.  What steps can you take to deepen your relationship with the Holy Spirit and recognize His voice more clearly?

column5: 4.  We should rely on the power of the Holy Spirit to step out boldly and fulfill the mission God has given us. What specific mission and focus has God given you?

column5: 5.  The Holy Spirit leads us to truth and discernment. In your life, are there areas where you need clarity or wisdom? How can you invite the Holy Spirit and allow Him to guide you?
